title: Whipping Johnny Dodds with Bechet at St. Catherine Hall
summary: Barnes and Bechet used to out-play Dodds, who was then with Oliver at St. Catherine Hall, and Barnes says Bechet was a pal.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Who were the guys that you used to think were tough, say in the 20s, that would give you a good battle on the blues in the 20s and the 30s, around and then?

Well, the best man I could see was Johnny. Johnny who? Johnny who? Oh, did you overhear him play? Oh yeah, Johnny played here. We used to whip Johnny. Me and Bichet. You heard him play? Oh, I hope. Before he left here.
Who was he playing with at the time you heard him? Who was he playing with? Playing with the, with the,

Stella Starr, not Stella Starr, Oliver. He was playing with Oliver. We used to go up at the St. Catherine Hall, that was their home and most of the time they played. St. Catherine Hall? St. Catherine Hall.
Where did charity edge down there? Charity? Where did you cross the street from the charity hospital? Yeah, yeah. That's the place.
Well now, how about some of these other fellas, Zeb and Charlie, did they play anything like Johnny Dives, would you say? Well, I don't know.

A toasting up is what it's like, Charlie. Not a toasting up was. A clamor is always just coming in something like with each other. Make no difference in one who's clamor, you see? Then we'll have something to sound like to each other. I see.
Yeah. Would you say he played a lot of blues, Johnny Dives?
Johnny Dives played a lot of blues. We used to grow up there and whip him out, me and Bichet.
Was he scared of y'all or were you scared of him?
Were you scared of Bichet yourself? We looked for him.
Were you scared of Bichet yourself?

No, I wasn't a player with Bichet. Bichet was more than me and we was pals. We used to come and get them, we'd talk, we'd take our clamor, ride them in the newspaper, put them on the back, bounce them, and go. Anyway, they was a good clamor player, we'd go.
